subject: science
prompt_en: Your mother bought a bag of moong that has small stones, some dust and bits of husk in it. Plan the steps to clean it.
prompt_hi: Mummy ne moong ka thaila khareeda jisme chhote kankar, thodi dhool aur bhoose ke tukde hain. Saaf karne ke steps plan karo.
answer: For example: winnow it (with a supa or in a breeze) to remove husk and dust; handpick the stones; sieve if fine dust remains; then wash it. Each step uses a different difference between the parts.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a winnowing scene: a farmer on a stool, an arrow for the wind, a heap of grain and a heap of husk. Label which heap is closer and why.
prompt_hi: Phatakne ka drishya banao: stool pe khada kisaan, hawa ka teer, anaaj ka dher aur bhoose ka dher. Likho kaunsa dher paas hai aur kyon.
answer: The grain heap is right below and close to the farmer; the husk heap is farther away in the direction of the wind, because husk is lighter.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'To separate black til from white til of the same size, I'll use a sieve.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Ek hi size ke kaale til aur safed til ko alag karne ke liye main chalni use karunga.' Galti kya hai?
answer: A sieve separates by size, and the seeds are the same size, so they would all pass through or all stay. Only colour differs, so handpicking is the simple method, though slow.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a city friend how grain gets from the field into a clean sack, using threshing and winnowing.
prompt_hi: Shehar ke dost ko samjhao ki anaaj khet se saaf bore tak kaise pahunchta hai, threshing aur winnowing ke saath.
answer: Key ideas: harvested stalks are threshed (beaten, or trampled or machine-crushed) to free the grain; the mixture is winnowed in the wind so the light husk blows away; remaining stones are handpicked or sieved; the clean grain is filled in sacks.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what is threshing?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: threshing (gahaai) kya hai?
answer: Beating or crushing harvested stalks to separate the grain from the stalks.

subject: science
prompt_en: How is tea separated from tea leaves when your family makes chai?
prompt_hi: Ghar pe chai banate waqt chai ko patti se kaise alag karte hain?
answer: By filtration (straining) through a tea strainer: the leaves stay in the strainer and the tea passes through.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you stir muddy water in a glass and leave it undisturbed for an hour. What will you see?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: glass mein matmaila paani hila ke ek ghante tak bina chhede rakho. Kya dikhega?
answer: The mud and sand settle at the bottom (sedimentation), with clearer water on top, though it may still be a little cloudy.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you pour salt water through a clean cloth or filter paper. Will the water coming out still be salty?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: namak wala paani saaf kapde ya filter paper se chhaano. Jo paani niklega, kya woh ab bhi namkeen hoga?
answer: Yes; the salt is dissolved and passes through the filter with the water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you leave a plate of salt water in the sun for two days. What will be left on the plate?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: namak wale paani ki plate do din dhoop mein rakho. Plate pe kya bachega?
answer: White salt crystals; the water has evaporated.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said salt passes through the filter. Why does a filter stop sand but not salt?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha namak filter se nikal jaata hai. Filter ret ko kyon rok leta hai par namak ko nahi?
answer: Sand grains are insoluble and too big to fit through the filter's tiny holes; dissolved salt is spread in the water as extremely tiny particles that pass through.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare sand-water and salt-water. Which can be separated by filtration, and which needs evaporation to get the solid back?
prompt_hi: Ret-paani aur namak-paani compare karo. Kise filtration se alag kar sakte hain, aur kise thos wapas paane ke liye evaporation chahiye?
answer: Sand-water: filtration (or sedimentation and decantation). Salt-water: evaporation, to get the salt back.

subject: science
prompt_en: When rice is washed before cooking, how does your family pour away the dirty water without losing the rice?
prompt_hi: Pakane se pehle chawal dhote waqt ghar wale ganda paani kaise phenkte hain bina chawal gire?
answer: They let the rice settle at the bottom and gently pour off the water: sedimentation and decantation.

subject: science
prompt_en: In the Rann of Kutch, salt farmers (agariyas) let salty water stand in wide, shallow pans for weeks. Why shallow pans, and why does salt appear?
prompt_hi: Rann of Kutch mein namak banane wale (agariya) namkeen paani ko chaude, uthle khetnuma kyaariyon mein hafton tak rehne dete hain. Uthli kyaariyan kyon, aur namak kyon dikhne lagta hai?
answer: Wide, shallow pans give a large surface area, so the sun and wind evaporate the water faster; the dissolved salt is left behind as crystals.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a filtration setup: a funnel, folded filter paper, a glass below, and muddy water being poured in. Label where the mud ends up and what drips into the glass.
prompt_hi: Filtration ka setup banao: funnel, mudha hua filter paper, neeche glass, aur daala jaata matmaila paani. Likho ki mitti kahan rukti hai aur glass mein kya tapakta hai.
answer: The mud stays on the filter paper (the residue); clearer water (the filtrate) drips into the glass.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'I'll make sea water drinkable by filtering it through my handkerchief.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Main samundar ke paani ko apne rumaal se chhaan ke peene layak bana doonga.' Galti kya hai?
answer: Filtering can't remove dissolved salt, so it would still be salty; removing salt needs evaporation with the vapour collected and cooled, or special purification.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend how to get cleaner water from muddy water using three methods in order, and whether it is then safe to drink.
prompt_hi: Ek dost ko samjhao ki matmaile paani se 3 tareekon se, sahi kram mein, saaf paani kaise milta hai, aur kya phir woh peene layak hai.
answer: Key ideas: sedimentation (let the mud settle), decantation (pour off the top), filtration (through cloth or filter paper); it may still have germs or dissolved substances, so boil or purify it before drinking.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: which method gets salt back from salt water?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: namak wale paani se namak wapas kaunsa tareeka deta hai?
answer: Evaporation.

subject: science
prompt_en: Sort these into living and non-living: a cow, a bicycle, a mango tree, a cloud, a mushroom, a stone.
prompt_hi: Inhe jeevit aur nirjeev mein baanto: gaay, cycle, aam ka ped, baadal, mushroom, patthar.
answer: Living: cow, mango tree, mushroom. Non-living: bicycle, cloud, stone.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you gently touch the leaves of a touch-me-not (chhui-mui, lajwanti) plant. What will happen, and what does it show?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: chhui-mui (lajwanti) ke patton ko halke se chhoo do. Kya hoga, aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: The leaflets quickly fold and droop; it shows that plants respond to touch, so they are living.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: you keep some dry chana in a dry box and some on wet cotton for three days. What will you see in each?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: kuch sookhe chane sookhe dabbe mein aur kuch geeli rui pe 3 din rakho. Dono mein kya dikhega?
answer: The chana on wet cotton swell and sprout; the ones in the dry box stay the same. Seeds are alive but resting.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: a potted plant is kept on a windowsill for a week without being turned. Which way will its shoot bend?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: gamle ka paudha ek hafte khidki pe bina ghumaye rakha hai. Uski tehni kis taraf jhukegi?
answer: Towards the light (the window); plants respond to light.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said the car is not living even though it moves. How did you decide?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha car chalti hai phir bhi jeevit nahi hai. Ye kaise decide kiya?
answer: Living things show all the features together; a car doesn't grow, reproduce, respire like living things or respond on its own, so moving alone isn't enough.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare a growing puppy with a diya flame you have seen. Both 'need air' and can get bigger. What makes only one of them living?
prompt_hi: Badhte hue pille aur kabhi dekhi diye ki lau compare karo. Dono ko 'hawa chahiye' aur dono bade ho sakte hain. Kya cheez sirf ek ko jeevit banaati hai?
answer: The puppy eats, grows into an adult by building its own body, respires, responds, will reproduce and has a life span. The flame isn't made of cells, doesn't feed and build a body, has no life cycle and doesn't produce young of its kind, so it is non-living.

subject: science
prompt_en: Is the mango tree in your colony living? Give three pieces of evidence.
prompt_hi: Kya tumhari colony ka aam ka ped jeevit hai? 3 saboot do.
answer: Yes. Any three: it grows taller and gets new leaves; it needs water and makes its own food; it respires; it flowers and makes fruits with seeds (reproduces); it responds to light; it will die one day.

subject: science
prompt_en: Scientists searching for life on Mars look for certain signs. What signs would tell them something is living?
prompt_hi: Mangal pe jeevan dhundhne wale vaigyanik kuch nishaaniyan dhundhte hain. Kaunsi nishaaniyan batayengi ki koi cheez jeevit hai?
answer: Signs that it takes in food or energy, grows, respires (exchanges gases), gets rid of wastes, responds to changes, and reproduces.

subject: science
prompt_en: Make a table with the features grows, needs food, respires, responds and reproduces as rows, and a cow, a mango tree and a car as columns. Fill in ✓ or ✗.
prompt_hi: Ek table banao: rows mein 'badhta hai, khaana chahiye, shwasan karta hai, pratikriya deta hai, prajanan karta hai', aur columns mein gaay, aam ka ped aur car. ✓ ya ✗ bharo.
answer: Cow: ✓ for all five. Mango tree: ✓ for all five. Car: ✗ for all five (fuel is not food, and it doesn't grow, respire, respond on its own or reproduce).

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu says: 'Plants are non-living because they can't walk, and dry seeds are dead.' What would you tell him?
prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Paudhe nirjeev hain kyonki chal nahi sakte, aur sookhe beej mare hue hote hain.' Tum use kya bataoge?
answer: Walking from place to place isn't needed: plants grow, respire, respond and reproduce, so they are living; seeds are alive but resting and sprout when given water, air and warmth.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how to decide whether something is living, using a seed and a toy car.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko beej aur khilone wali car ke example se samjhao ki koi cheez jeevit hai ya nahi, kaise decide karein.
answer: Key ideas: check all the features together; a seed came from a parent plant, respires slowly, grows into a plant when given water, air and warmth, and that plant makes new seeds, so it is living; a toy car may move but doesn't grow, eat, respire or reproduce, so it is non-living.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name one way a plant shows that it responds to its surroundings.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek tareeka batao jisse paudha dikhata hai ki woh aas-paas ke badlaav pe pratikriya deta hai.
answer: Any one: touch-me-not leaves fold when touched; shoots bend towards light; roots grow towards water; some flowers open in the day and close at night.

subject: science
prompt_en: You want to test whether seeds need water. Describe the two sets you will make and what stays the same.
prompt_hi: Tum test karna chahte ho ki kya beejon ko paani chahiye. Kaunse do set banaoge aur kya same rakhoge?
answer: Set A: seeds on dry cotton. Set B: seeds on wet cotton. Keep the same: kind and number of seeds, container, place and warmth; compare after 3-4 days.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: moong seeds on wet cotton are kept in a dark cupboard, and another set in a sunny window. Will both sprout?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: geeli rui pe moong ek andhere almari mein aur doosra set dhoop wali khidki pe rakha hai. Kya dono ankurit honge?
answer: Yes, both sprout; light isn't needed for germination. (Later, the dark ones grow pale and long.)

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: set 1 of seeds stays fully under water for 4 days; set 2 sits on wet cotton. Which sprouts better?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: set 1 ke beej 4 din poore paani mein doobe rehte hain; set 2 geeli rui pe hai. Kaun behtar ankurit hoga?
answer: Set 2; seeds kept fully under water get too little air, so they germinate poorly or not at all.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: seeds on wet cotton are kept in the fridge, and another set on the kitchen shelf, for 3 days. What happens?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: geeli rui pe beej 3 din fridge mein, aur doosra set rasoi ki shelf pe. Kya hoga?
answer: The shelf seeds sprout; the fridge seeds sprout very slowly or not at all, because it is too cold.

subject: science
prompt_en: You said seeds sprout even in a dark box. Why don't they need sunlight yet?
prompt_hi: Tumne kaha beej andhere dabbe mein bhi ankurit hote hain. Unhe abhi dhoop ki zaroorat kyon nahi?
answer: The seed has food stored inside it for its first growth; light is needed later, when the leaves start making food.

subject: science
prompt_en: After a week, seedlings grown in a dark box look pale yellow and long; those grown near a window are green and short. What does this tell you?
prompt_hi: Ek hafte baad, andhere dabbe ke paudhe peele aur lambe dikhte hain; khidki ke paas wale hare aur chhote. Isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Light isn't needed for germination, but young plants need light to grow healthy green leaves and make food; in the dark they stretch, looking for light, and stay pale.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do farmers sow many seeds after the first monsoon rains and not in dry soil?
prompt_hi: Kisaan bahut se beej pehli monsoon baarish ke baad kyon bote hain, sookhi mitti mein kyon nahi?
answer: Seeds need water to germinate; the rain wets the soil, and it is warm too.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your class wants to test whether warmth affects how fast seeds sprout. Plan a fair test with what you have at home, without any heater or flame.
prompt_hi: Tumhari class test karna chahti hai ki kya garmi se beej jaldi ankurit hote hain. Ghar ki cheezon se, bina heater ya aag ke, ek fair test plan karo.
answer: Two identical containers with the same number and kind of seeds on equally wet cotton; cover both so the light is the same; keep one in a warm spot in the house and one in the fridge; count sprouted seeds each day and repeat the test.

subject: science
prompt_en: Riya's sprouting record for 10 seeds on wet cotton: Day 1: 0, Day 2: 3, Day 3: 8, Day 4: 10. Her dry set stayed at 0 every day. Draw a bar or line graph and tell me what it shows.
prompt_hi: Riya ka record, geeli rui pe 10 beej: Din 1: 0, Din 2: 3, Din 3: 8, Din 4: 10. Uska sookha set har din 0 raha. Bar ya line graph banao aur batao isse kya pata chalta hai.
answer: The wet set rises to 10 by day 4 while the dry set stays at 0; seeds need water to germinate.

subject: science
prompt_en: Golu tests water: wet seeds in a warm room and dry seeds in the fridge. He says, 'Water is needed.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Golu paani ka test karta hai: geele beej garam kamre mein aur sookhe beej fridge mein. Woh kehta hai, 'Paani zaroori hai.' Galti kya hai?
answer: He changed both water and temperature, so it's an unfair test; he should keep both sets in the same place and change only the water.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to your mother why moong sprouts in a wet cloth without soil or sunlight, and why the sprouts must not be left under water.
prompt_hi: Mummy ko samjhao ki moong geele kapde mein bina mitti ya dhoop ke kyon ankurit hota hai, aur ankur ko paani mein dooba kar kyon nahi chhodna chahiye.
answer: Key ideas: seeds need water, air and warmth; they have stored food, so they don't need soil or light to sprout; kept fully under water they get too little air and sprout poorly.
